title: Actions and naturality of the balanced derived tensor model
statement: For the balanced model $P\otimes_R F$ of $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ [lem-pc-balanced-derived-tensor-model], multiplication by $a\in A$ on $P$ induces the action of the corresponding endomorphism of $M$ in $D(A)$; each $b\in R'$ acts on $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ through the endomorphism of $R'$ in $D(R)$ given by multiplication by $b$, and these commuting actions make every $H^i(P\otimes_R F)$ an $A\otimes_R R'$-module. The canonical isomorphisms between the models for different choices of $P$ and $F$, and their identification with $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$, are $A\otimes_R R'$-linear on cohomology and natural in $M$; and under them the canonical comparison map $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'\to M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(A\otimes_R R')$ is represented by the chain map $P\otimes_R F\to P\otimes_R R'=P\otimes_A(A\otimes_R R')$ induced by $F\to R'$, whose effect on each $H^i$ is $A\otimes_R R'$-linear.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-balanced-derived-tensor-model] to obtain T, its counit alpha, the unique specified model isomorphisms, the coefficient ring maps rho, and the pure-tensor cohomology actions. Choose these witnesses inside the theorem proof; no new definition chooses data from an unproved existence theorem.

For a chain map g, the naturality square of T.map(Q.map(g)) commutes with each second-factor multiplication. Apply homology. Since its map is A-linear, the pure-tensor action formula gives tensor-ring linearity for a tensor a tensor b; tensor induction proves it for every scalar.

For the specified model isomorphism e, cancel the invertible K-flat counit. The naturality equation of alpha, A-linearity of the resolution q, functoriality of T, and naturality of T.map(Q.map(q)) prove the first-factor scalar equation. Transfer the cohomology module structure along the additive equivalence of H(e); its linearity is the inverse-equivalence identity.

At E=R-prime[0], let v be the component of T.map(Q.map(q)) and put c=v inverse followed by alpha_P at E. The quasi-isomorphism q makes v invertible. Cancel the counit at F, use the defining equation of e, and apply naturality of T.map(Q.map(q)) and alpha to f to show e followed by c equals Q(P tensor f). The same naturality squares for multiplication by b show rho_M(b) followed by c equals c followed by the target multiplication.

For the target, the additive composite of single complexes, underived total tensor, localization and homology sends the multiplication ring map of R-prime to A-linear endomorphisms. Its restriction to R is the A-scalar map: check extension of scalars on tensors 1 tensor x and the total complex on its summand inclusions; use the natural homology comparison with ordinary complex homology to preserve scalars. The algebra tensor universal property gives the target cohomology module with the required pure-tensor formula. A-linearity of H(c), its second-ring equivariance, and tensor induction establish the final linearity clause.
